title: Sable and the Spire
premise: Coral Okafor has spent nine years guarding the Thornfell gate, feeding the wards with small, deliberate sacrifices of their own memory so no one notices the border exists at all. When the stars go out and the wards collapse in a single night, Coral learns the truth: the gate was never keeping smugglers out—it was keeping the Hollow King's hunger in, and the thing wearing the crown of Sable has been eating memories to grow strong enough to break free. Guided by a disgraced royal cartographer, a star-child who fell from the darkened sky, and the ghost of the gate's first keeper, Coral must journey to the Spire and unbind the true king before his stolen memories—including every trace of Coral's own past—are consumed forever. In the end, Coral defeats the Hollow King not by destroying him but by giving back what he lost, choosing to forget themselves entirely so the king can remember who he is; the found family they made along the way becomes the keeper of Coral's story, promising to tell it until Coral can be found again.
about_author: Marguerite Almeida is a former lighthouse keeper turned novelist who writes fantasy about thresholds—doors, borders, and the people paid to stand between. She lives on a fog-bound coast with her partner, two opinionated cats, and an ever-growing map of imaginary mountains.

chapters.title: The Toll of Small Things
chapters.summary: Coral Okafor's POV. On an ordinary night at the Thornfell gate, Coral pays the ward-toll—a memory of their mother's voice—and logs a routine smuggler sighting. The chapter establishes the quiet rhythm of invisible service and ends with Coral noticing one wrong detail: the stars over the pass have begun to flicker like dying candles. Emotional beat: loneliness worn as duty.

chapters.title: When the Sky Went Dark
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The stars go out all at once, and the wards shatter like glass. A wounded stranger crashes through the broken gate: Wren, a star-child who fell from the extinguished sky and carries a shard of light in her chest. Smugglers close in behind her, hunting the light. Coral breaks nine years of neutrality to save her. Emotional beat: terror cracking open into choice.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Confession
chapters.summary: Alternating Coral and Wren POVs. They shelter with Idris Vane, a disgraced royal cartographer living in exile, whose forbidden maps show the Spire and a route no one survives. Idris reveals the border wards were built by the crown itself—to cage something. He agrees to guide them, ashamed he helped draw the prison. Emotional beat: guilt seeking redemption.

chapters.title: What the Gate Kept
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. The ghost of Maren Solenne, the gate's first keeper, manifests from the ruined wards and tells the truth: the 'king' of Sable died decades ago, and something called the Hollow King wears his crown, devouring memories to grow. Every ward-toll Coral ever paid fed it. Coral realizes their forgotten past is inside the enemy. Emotional beat: horror of complicity.

chapters.title: Smuggler's Road
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The three travel the hidden roads Coral knows by body even where memory fails them, pursued by the Hollow King's hollowed soldiers—people emptied of everything but obedience. A ambush costs them their supplies, and Wren's light-shard begins to dim, meaning she is fading. Emotional beat: found family forming under fire.

chapters.title: The City That Forgot Itself
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. They reach Greyhollow, a city whose people have been partially devoured—citizens who cannot recall their own names, moving through rituals they no longer understand. Here Coral meets a hollowed woman who almost remembers being Coral's mother, forcing Coral to confront what the tolls truly cost. Emotional beat: grief for a self already half-erased.

chapters.title: Bargain at the Ash Chapel
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. To reach the Spire, they need passage across the Ashlands, held by the smuggler-queen Veska, whom Coral once betrayed. Veska offers passage in exchange for Wren's light-shard. Coral refuses; Idris secretly considers accepting. The group fractures over what survival is worth. Emotional beat: trust tested against desperation.

chapters.title: The Price Already Paid
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Hollowed soldiers corner them in the Ashlands; Maren's ghost burns out holding the line, and Idris takes a mortal wound buying time. Dying, he gives Coral his master map and confesses the final secret: the Spire's door only opens to someone willing to be wholly forgotten. Emotional beat: sacrifice transforming guilt into purpose.

chapters.title: The Hollow Crown
chapters.summary: Coral and Wren's alternating POV. At the Spire's summit, Coral faces the Hollow King and finds him not monstrous but starving—a guardian, like Coral, who paid too many tolls and forgot why he guarded anything. Wren offers her last light; Coral offers the ultimate price: their entire remaining self. Emotional beat: climax as compassion rather than conquest.

chapters.title: Keeper of the Story
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The Hollow King remembers himself, the stars reignite, and Wren rises home carrying Coral's name like a lantern. In the aftermath, Wren chooses to stay in the world instead, joining Veska's reformed company to guard the healed gate. Each dawn she tells Coral's story aloud, waiting for a stranger with familiar eyes to come down the mountain. Emotional beat: mourning braided with hope.
